clue.text: Constraint of university wearing specified clothing

indicators.note: one piece wears the other, so the clothing word is put around the university letter

parts.note: a dress code names the clothing required, so specified clothing is dress

explanation.surface: A student feels hemmed in by a college that insists on a strict dress code.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is compulsion or coercion, a constraint forced upon someone.

clue.text: A graduate society in time could be held on computer

indicators.note: the graduate and society letters sit inside the word for a time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate's degree

explanation.surface: A graduate society keeps its records, given time, on a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'heid' is a misread of 'held'.
explanation.definitionFit: A database is a structured store of records kept and searched electronically.

clue.text: No waterer is prepared for this rose family member

indicators.note: the letters of no waterer are prepared, that is made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A gardener who never waters is ready to plant a hardy shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, belongs to the Rosaceae, the botanical rose family.

clue.text: Heads of scientific or health organisations in London district

indicators.note: the heads of the four words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: The chiefs of research and health bodies are based in a part of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a lively district of London's West End, known for restaurants and nightlife.

clue.text: Resentful, having committed an illegal act

definitions.meaning: feeling hurt or insulted by something
past form of the verb meaning to break the law

explanation.surface: A convicted criminal is bitter about the sentence for the crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurt feelings and breaking the law are both senses of the verb, here in its past participle.

clue.text: He's certainly not in at present

definitions.text: He's certainly not in at present

parts.words: He's certainly not in at present
parts.note: in cricket the side that is in is batting; a player in the other side, out on the field, is not in

explanation.surface: Someone calling at a house is told the man of the house is out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone absent from home; in cricket the team 'in' is batting, so a player of the fielding side is never 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket player on the side not batting stands out in the field to stop and catch the ball.

clue.text: Demonstratively handling live fuse — iffy? Not half!

indicators.note: the letters are handled and moved about into a new order
half of the word iffy is dropped, its first half, leaving only its second half

explanation.surface: Someone gushes nervously while handling a dodgy live fuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' leaves FY from IFFY; 'handling' rearranges LIVE, FUSE and FY together.
explanation.definitionFit: To act effusively is to show feelings openly and gushingly, which is acting demonstratively.

clue.text: Smoothed ground with end first for one-time bowler

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is brought round to the front

parts.note: to rake soil is to level and smooth it

explanation.surface: A cricket groundsman prepared the pitch for a former bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Francis Drake is said to have finished his game of bowls on Plymouth Hoe before facing the Spanish Armada; the surface wants a cricket bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elizabethan seafarer is famed in legend as a player of bowls, so a bowler of long ago.

clue.text: Chaff to clear in the river

indicators.note: the word for clear goes inside the river name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
to rid a place of something is to clear it

explanation.surface: Husks from threshing are to be swept away into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chaff' looks like the noun for husks; here it is the verb meaning to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaff someone is to tease or mock them, as to deride is to ridicule.

clue.text: Public outcry covering the source of a metal

parts.note: fur is an animal's covering
ore is the rock from which a metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Protesters rage against a mining firm extracting metal from the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A furore is an outburst of public anger or excitement, an uproar.

clue.text: Time to possess accommodation that's modern, in a terrace?

parts.note: to own something is to possess it
a house provides accommodation

explanation.surface: A buyer finds time to own a modern home in a terraced row.
explanation.definitionFit: Developers now sell new terraced homes in town under this name, a modern dwelling built in a row.

clue.text: The tree outside the city shows artistic ability ?

indicators.note: the tree's letters stand outside the city's, enclosing them

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree
LA, Los Angeles, is a common crossword city

explanation.surface: A tree planted on the city's edge reveals someone's gift for art.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is a natural talent or stylish aptitude, as for art.

clue.text: Financial centre seen by the river

definitions.meaning: the sloping ground along the side of a river

explanation.surface: A city's money district stands beside the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a money-lending institution and the land edging a river.

clue.text: Deign to go down after study

indicators.note: the word for go down comes after the study word in the answer

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
to descend is to go down

explanation.surface: A scholar agrees reluctantly to come downstairs after hours of study.
explanation.definitionFit: To condescend is to stoop to do something thought beneath one, to deign.

clue.text: Island railway to carry lady evangelist

indicators.note: in a down clue the carrier holds up what it carries, so the lady sits on top

parts.note: miss is a title for a young lady
Iona is a Hebridean island famed for its early Christian abbey

explanation.surface: A train on an island carries a female preacher.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the island and railway carry the lady above them. Iona is a Scottish island where St Columba founded a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: A missionary spreads a faith, as an evangelist preaches the gospel.

clue.text: Mends, ie darns close knit item?

indicators.note: the letters are mended, that is reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: A housewife mends things and darns a closely knitted garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close knit' suggests knitting; it refers to fish packed tightly together in a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardines are proverbially packed tightly, so a sardine is jokingly close-knit.

clue.text: American patriot to regard with respect

definitions.meaning: Paul ..., who rode to warn of British troops in 1775
to hold in deep respect or esteem

explanation.surface: Americans honour a hero of their revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is that of a celebrated Revolutionary War rider, and the verb means to venerate.

clue.text: It's a defensive element to bring up one on a train

parts.note: to rear children is to bring them up
a guard travels on a train in charge of it

explanation.surface: A soldier is posted to raise one on a troop train as protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard is a body of troops protecting the back of an army, a defensive part.

clue.text: Harshly cut off, see

parts.note: to sever is to cut off
a see is a bishop's seat; Ely in Cambridgeshire is a cathedral city and see

explanation.surface: Someone is curtly told to cut contact and watch out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is not the verb to look; it is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is the crossword's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To act severely is to act with strictness or harshness.

clue.text: Little accommodation in county and centre of city

parts.note: Beds is the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county

indicators.note: the centre of a four-letter word is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: Cheap lodging is found in the county town's centre.
explanation.walkthrough: BEDS is short for Bedfordshire, an English county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a single rented room serving as bedroom and living space, small accommodation.

clue.text: Hurry! Sink's bunged up It'll cause irritation

parts.note: to tear along is to hurry

indicators.note: to bung is to throw, and in a down entry throwing up turns the word upward, reading backwards

parts.note: to sag is to sink or droop

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to hurry because a blocked sink is causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunged up' suggests a blocked sink; it means thrown up, turning SAG upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Police tear gas irritates the eyes and throat, disabling a crowd.

clue.text: Varied art collection

parts.note: a picture made by gathering assorted scraps and sticking them together

explanation.surface: A gallery shows a mixed collection of artworks.
explanation.definitionFit: A collage is an artwork assembled from assorted pieces of paper, fabric and photographs.

clue.text: Yarn about fishing tackle around the west

indicators.note: the fishing tackle word goes around the letter for west

parts.note: a creel is an angler's wicker basket for the catch
W is the abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: An angler spins a tale about tackle used out west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' suggests a tale; it is a wool thread used for embroidery.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewel is a fine worsted wool yarn used in embroidery.

clue.text: One of two first going in for the bottle?

definitions.text: One of two first going in
definitions.meaning: in cricket each side's first two batsmen go in to bat together
a tool used to take the cap off a bottle

explanation.surface: A drinker wonders who goes in first to get at the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening batsman starts a cricket innings, and a bottle tool removes caps.

clue.text: Alter soaps in switch to rural musical plays

indicators.note: the letters are put into a switch, changing their order

explanation.surface: A broadcaster swaps its soap operas for countryside musical dramas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alter' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the letters; 'in switch' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastorales are operatic or musical stage works on country themes.

clue.text: Blemishes arising in a thin tube

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: warts are small growths that blemish the skin

explanation.surface: Spots appear on a thin pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking straw is a narrow hollow tube for sipping.

clue.text: Fuzzy, losing head in a fever

indicators.note: the word drops its opening letter

parts.note: vague means fuzzy or unclear

explanation.surface: A patient's head goes fuzzy with a temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old name for malarial fever with shivering fits.

clue.text: KO with second barrel

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel

explanation.surface: A boxer is knocked out by a second blow, flattened like a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock someone out, or knock them senseless, is to stun them.

clue.text: It's not quite usual for this girl to appear

indicators.note: the word is not complete, missing its final letter

parts.note: normal means usual

explanation.surface: It is unusual for a certain young woman to turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a girl's name, as in Bellini's opera heroine.

clue.text: He has a superior view to the others at Cruft's

definitions.text: He has a superior view to the others at Cruft's

parts.words: He has a superior view to the others at Cruft's
parts.note: a very tall breed of dog, looking down on rival breeds at the famous British dog show

explanation.surface: A snobbish exhibitor looks down on rivals at a dog show.
explanation.walkthrough: Crufts is Britain's best-known dog show; 'superior view' means a higher vantage point, not snobbery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is one of the tallest dog breeds, so it literally looks down on others.

clue.text: Poor DIY in scraps beginning to mean disorderliness

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the word for scraps

parts.note: rows and scraps are both quarrels or fights

indicators.note: poor work is badly put together, so the letters are reworked
the beginning of the next word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Shoddy home improvements cause rows, the start of mean behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scraps' suggests leftovers, but here it means fights; 'Poor' shuffles the three DIY letters before they go in.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdyism is rough, noisy behaviour, a kind of disorder.

clue.text: Deano confused with year in the future

indicators.note: the name's letters are confused, mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Deano gets muddled about the year it will happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Some time ahead, at an unspecified point, is what the phrase means.
